subject: history
title: Charter Acts (1773-1853)
description: Regulating Act 1773, Pitt's India Act 1784, Charter Acts of 1793, 1813, 1833, 1853

content.overview: Charter Acts were passed by the British Parliament to renew the charter of the East India Company and regulate its affairs in India.
keyPoints: Regulating Act 1773: First step to control EIC, created Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings), Supreme Court at Calcutta
Pitt's India Act 1784: Established Board of Control, dual government system, Governor-General became Crown's representative
Charter Act 1793: Renewed EIC trade monopoly, Governor-General's power increased
Charter Act 1813: Ended EIC trade monopoly (except tea and trade with China), allowed Christian missionaries, allocated Rs. 1 lakh for education
Charter Act 1833: Centralized administration, Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck), ended EIC commercial activities, first Indian Law Commission
Charter Act 1853: Separated legislative and executive functions, introduced open competition for civil services, added 6 members to Governor-General's Council

mnemonics.explanation: 1813 Act allowed Christian missionaries and allocated Rs. 1 lakh for education

quiz.question: Which act created the post of Governor-General of Bengal?
quiz.explanation: Regulating Act 1773 created the post of Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings)

quiz.question: Which act ended EIC's trade monopoly?
quiz.explanation: Charter Act 1813 ended EIC's trade monopoly (except tea and China trade)

quiz.question: Pitt's India Act 1784 established:
quiz.explanation: Pitt's India Act 1784 established the Board of Control
